description:
FOUND s495 (Fable, 2026-09-21) while writing the s492b review probes (the probe itself tripped it).  PRE-EXISTING on main 99868bb1 (= 88e99ef8's code).  LOUD (the whole file is refused at transpile), not silent.
REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs main; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/review/s492b/cap1.pl + ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/probes/c3..c11.pl):
  sub op { open(my $h, "<", $0) or die; $h }
  my $h = 5; print "ok $h\n";                      perl: ok 5      PCL: Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'h' captured by sub op
THE SHAPE, measured (9 probes): a NAMED sub (or an anon sub inside one, c9) that DECLARES a lexical with an EMBEDDED `my` -- inside a call's arguments `open(my $h, ...)` / `opendir(my $d, ...)` / `id(my $h = 2)`, a condition `if ((my $h = 1) > 0)`, a loop head `while (my $h = shift)` -- AND USES it afterwards in the sub, PLUS a file-level STATEMENT `my $h` of the same name declared LATER in the file.  All five spellings refuse.
WHAT DOES NOT TRIP IT (so the detector's blind spot is exactly the embedded declaration): a statement-level `my $h = 1;` in the sub (cap2: fine); the file-level `my $h` declared BEFORE the sub (c5: fine -- the sub's own `$h` is correctly its own); the file-level declaration itself embedded, `open(my $fh, ">", ...)` at file level after `sub read_file { open(my $fh, ...) ... }` (c10: fine -- which is why the everyday slurp-helper script works); a sub whose embedded `my` is never USED again in the sub (c11: fine).  0 hits in the 122-program everyday seed corpus and 0 in the 655 Rosetta programs: RARE, which is the only reason this is not urgent.
MECHANISM (not measured beyond the shape -- measure first): the capture DETECTOR (`_check_sub_captures`, Pl/Parser2.pm) asks whether the sub's block DECLARES the name and evidently only counts a `PPI::Statement::Variable`; an embedded `my` is a Token::Word inside an expression, so the use after it looks like a free reference to the (later-promoted) file lexical.  Siblings already fixed the same way: #272 (embedded `my` in an ANON sub body), #454 (a signature parameter is a declaration).  STANDING RULE: a SCOPE-blind capture refusal is a BUG -- and detector / rewriter / promoter must share ONE resolver: fixing the detector alone would turn the refusal into a SILENT WRONG if the REWRITER (`_ref_shadowed` -> `_stmt_declares_canon`) then renames the sub's `$h` to the file lexical's cell.  Check both ask the same question (#454 is the worked example), and that the embedded `my`'s scope starts where perl's does (the declaring STATEMENT's successor for call args; the condition + branches for `if`; the head + body for `while`).
BAR: a name-resolution change => the FULL SWEEP is the gate + `--quick` companion once + the gate-SET scan over both populations (a refusal stops firing: s372 rule); guard rows (the five spellings + the four negatives above, inverse-verified on the base) in a capture/scoping Pl/t file; corpus-diff + emission-ab expected IDENTICAL (no corpus file has the shape -- if so, say so).
subject: BUG (loud, pre-existing, rare): a sub that declares a lexical with an EMBEDDED `my` -- `open(my $h, ...)`, `if ((my $h = ...))`, `while (my $h = ...)`, `f(my $h = ...)` -- and uses it, plus a LATER file-level `my $h`, refuses the WHOLE FILE: "Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'h' captured by sub op" -- the capture detector does not count an embedded `my` as a declaration (#272 / #454 family)
